title: Residue fields of finite type schemes have finite transcendence degree
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$. Then the transcendence degree [def-kun-transcendence-degree] $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)$ of the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] is finite.

source.place: Lemma \"lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring\" (Tag 00P0), applied to A/p on an affine neighbourhood of x

proof.text: Apply the finite-type definition to the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and choose a member $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of its finite-type affine cover containing $x$; thus $A=K[a_1,\ldots,a_n]$. The point $x$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$. In the construction of the affine structure sheaf (Stacks Tag 01HU, definition-structure-sheaf), sections on $D(s)$ are $A_s$; these opens with $s\notin\mathfrak p$ form a neighbourhood basis. Taking germs therefore gives $\mathcal O_{X,x}=A_{\mathfrak p}$: a germ is a fraction $a/s$, and two such fractions agree precisely after multiplying their cross-difference by some $t\notin\mathfrak p$. Its maximal ideal consists of fractions with numerator in $\mathfrak p$, so the map $a/s\mapsto\bar a/\bar s$ induces $\kappa(x)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}\cong\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$: it is surjective since every nonzero denominator in $A/\mathfrak p$ lifts outside $\mathfrak p$, and its kernel is exactly $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$. Every element is thus a quotient of polynomials in the images $\bar a_i$, so this field equals $K(\bar a_1,\ldots,\bar a_n)$ as a field extension via the structure morphism.

source.place: Tag 01HU, definition-structure-sheaf, and its preceding construction on standard opens; Tag 00P0, algebra.tex lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring, applied to A/𝔭.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] to the field extension $\kappa(x)/K$ generated by the finitely many images $\bar a_i$ from Step 1. It gives a finite transcendence basis $B$. By [def-kun-transcendence-degree], $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)=|B|$, which is finite. An empty basis gives degree zero; if $X$ is empty there is no point to check.

source.place: Tag 030F, lemma-transcendence-degree, proof: a transcendence basis can be chosen inside a generating set.
